subject.title: [Slack] Agent lacks visibility into own channel messages from DM sessions

question: Should Slack DM turns receive a narrowly scoped record of the same agent’s outbound channel activity, and what authorization/account/channel scope must apply before any content is returned?
rationale: The correct answer determines whether the implementation is a self-only activity ledger, an explicitly scoped session-history capability, or no cross-session recall at all; code cannot safely choose that privacy boundary.

options.title: Approve scoped self-activity recall
options.body: Add a Slack-owned, same-agent/account activity record that exposes only the agent’s outbound channel messages with destination metadata to authorized DM turns.

options.title: Keep session isolation strict
options.body: Retain current session separation and document that cross-context recall is intentionally unavailable unless a future explicit capability is designed.

options.title: Design a generic session-history capability
options.body: Create a broader SDK-level authorization contract only if maintainers want configurable cross-session history beyond Slack self-activity.

recommendation.title: Approve scoped self-activity recall
recommendation.body: Add a Slack-owned, same-agent/account activity record that exposes only the agent’s outbound channel messages with destination metadata to authorized DM turns.

likelyOwner.reason: The discussion and feature history place steipete closest to the Slack routing, outbound-session, and privacy-boundary decision.
